comparison: Perfect agreement on C34-C47. Both evaluations find the model well-constrained by experimental data and successfully reproducing key features of pDp. Reviewers explicitly praised the biological realism that OpenEval documented.

Partial overlap on C51-C52 (assembly creation and instability). OpenEval focuses on methodology and network properties, while peer review (R2) groups these claims with broader findings about Scaled I network instability (C11-C12, C53-C55, C109, C111-C112). Both accept the instability findings.

Partial overlap on C53-C55 (E/I correlations and Scaled I network limitations). OpenEval R3 focuses on E/I correlation measurements and experimental comparison, while peer R2 groups these with broader instability findings. Both accept that Scaled I networks fail to match experimental observations.

Partial overlap on C56-C57, C60 (co-tuning metrics and functional consequences). OpenEval R3 includes these with E/I correlation analysis, while peer R3 groups them with stabilization effects (C13-C15, C58-C59, C113). Both find the evidence compelling.

Partial overlap on C58-C59 (firing rate properties of Tuned networks). OpenEval R4 focuses specifically on firing rate comparisons, while peer R3 integrates these with broader stabilization findings. Both accept the demonstrated differences between network types.

Partial overlap on C11-C12 (core findings about E/I assemblies on network dynamics). OpenEval R5 focuses on the computational simulation results, while peer R2 groups these with instability findings. Both accept the core findings as demonstrated.

Partial overlap on C13-C15 (E/I assembly effects). OpenEval R5 presents these as core findings with acknowledged mechanistic gaps, while peer R3 groups them with stabilization evidence and praises the mechanistic explanations. Both support the findings.

Strong agreement on C62-C65 (network dynamics and attractor characterization). Both evaluations accept the findings about transient dynamics versus persistent activity. Peer review explicitly notes this contributes to understanding alternatives to traditional attractor networks.

Partial overlap on C67-C70 (pattern completion behavior). OpenEval R7 provides detailed analysis of pattern completion across network types, while peer R5 accepts these findings as part of the broader narrative. Both note the absence of classical pattern completion in Tuned networks.

Partial overlap on C79-C81 (geometric transformations and local curvature). OpenEval R8 focuses on odor representation geometry, while peer R6 emphasizes the novelty of local manifold projections. Both find the geometric findings compelling and well-supported.

Partial overlap on C85 (local manifold hypothesis). OpenEval R9 presents dimensionality analysis supporting this hypothesis, while peer R6 praises it as novel and intriguing. Both accept the manifold interpretation.

Strong agreement on C82-C84 (dimensionality analysis). Both evaluations accept the participation ratio measurements and their interpretation as supporting intermediate representations between high-dimensional and discrete attractors.

Perfect agreement on C86-C93 (detailed manifold geometry characterization). Both evaluations praise the mechanistic analysis of bidirectional effects (amplification and suppression). Peer review explicitly commends the mechanistic explanations.

Perfect agreement on C94 (robustness controls). Both evaluations explicitly praise this analysis for demonstrating that results stem from connectivity structure rather than specific biophysical parameters.

Strong overlap on C96-C102 (pattern classification enhancement). OpenEval finds the evidence well-supported with appropriate nuance (C102). Peer review raises concern that classification advantage may be context-dependent and that Tuned networks trade salience for stability, suggesting limitations not fully captured in OpenEval's assessment.

Perfect agreement on C103-C105 (concentration estimation). Both evaluations accept the findings as demonstrating additional computational capabilities beyond classification, consistent with the functional advantages of E/I assemblies.

Perfect agreement on C106-C108 (continual learning). Both evaluations accept the findings while implicitly acknowledging the limited scope (only two additional assemblies). Both find the stability benefits demonstrated.

Partial overlap on C109, C111-C112 (global inhibition failure). OpenEval R15 synthesizes findings about network stability, while peer R2 groups these with broader instability findings. Both accept that global inhibition fails to provide stability.

Partial overlap on C113 (E/I assembly success). OpenEval R15 includes this in synthesis of key findings, while peer R3 groups it with stabilization evidence. Both accept the demonstrated success of E/I assemblies.

Partial overlap on C114 (E/I assemblies and manifold geometry). OpenEval R15 includes this in synthesis, while peer R6 emphasizes it as part of the novel geometric findings. Both accept the connection between E/I structure and manifold formation.

Perfect agreement on C119-C121 (consistency with experimental observations). Both evaluations accept that the model's predictions align with biological observations of irregular, transient activity, supporting the model's validity.

Partial overlap on C16 (manifold geometry summary). OpenEval R19 summarizes key findings about geometric transformations, while peer R6 praises these as novel and convincing. Both support the geometric findings.

Partial overlap on C17 (classification enhancement summary). OpenEval R19 summarizes functional consequences of geometry, while peer R9 raises concerns about context-dependence of classification advantages. Divergence in assessment of generality.

Perfect agreement on C20-C22 (functional implications). OpenEval marks C21-C22 as uncertain/speculative due to limited testing, while peer review accepts these as reasonable extrapolations about functional significance. Both acknowledge speculative nature of higher-order learning claims.

OpenEval R16 addresses C115-C118 (theoretical context and parameter space exploration). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These claims about theoretical consistency and parameter continuum were not explicitly discussed in peer reviews.
OpenEval R18 addresses C122 (theoretical justification for modeling approach). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. This theoretical framing was not explicitly discussed in peer reviews.

OpenEval R21 addresses C1-C10 (biological foundation through experimental citations). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviews implicitly accepted the biological grounding by praising the model's experimental constraints.

OpenEval R22 addresses C23-C33 (theoretical and experimental context from literature). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These background claims were not explicitly evaluated in peer reviews.
